A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PHAT and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Relocated sections and renumbered tables can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on 14 real-world datasets and a synthetic dataset, alongside ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains the original forecasting results, synthetic-data comparison, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same FFT-based period detection, bucket construction, positive-negative attention, nonperiodic-bucket handling, and prediction fusion. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 14 real-world datasets and the synthetic sequence combining ETTh1 and ETTm1. Forecasting tasks and periodicity scenarios remain unchanged; newly cited applications are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmarks, fixed-input comparison, periodicity-model comparison, and attention-variant comparison. The expanded bibliography introduces no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, look-back ranges, forecasting horizons, MSE/MAE metrics, and training settings match. The fixed-input experiment moves from v1 Section 4.3 to v3 Appendix D.3 with identical settings.

E4.justification: Figure 3 retains the component ablations and layer/period-count sensitivity analyses. Figures 4–6 and Tables 8–10 retain the same periodicity visualizations, synthetic comparison, attention comparisons, and detailed ablations.

E5.justification: Both retain the 95% autocorrelation confidence bands described in Figure 1. Neither reports forecasting run counts, seeds, or uncertainty intervals, and no statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All ten tables match after accounting for renumbering, and the figure results are unchanged. For example, fixed-input ETTh1 PHAT MSE/MAE remain 0.375/0.389 in v1 Table 3 and v3 Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is unchanged, including Appendix C's period-heterogeneity definition, stick-breaking proposition and proof, allocation bounds, and variance argument. Equations 1–28 are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same novelty, periodic-bucket, signed-attention, efficiency, and forecasting-performance claims. The claimed evaluation scope remains 14 real-world datasets and 18 baselines.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning periodic interference, negative-path gating, nonperiodic inputs, and differences from patch-based methods remain unchanged. The fixed-input fairness discussion is relocated without substantive revision; no new limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same PyTorch implementation, A100 80 GB hardware, optimization details, and dataset-specific hyperparameters. v1 Table 5 becomes v3 Table 4 unchanged, and the embedded GitHub code link is identical.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix A substantially broaden the cited research context across architectures, channel interactions, optimization, inference, and additional applications. Added works include Timebase, Timefilter, DBLoss, and test-time learning; several earlier survey and recurrent-network references disappear. PHAT's central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The fixed-input subsection moves to Appendix D.3, with corresponding section-reference updates. Appendix A receives limited prose expansion; author order, contact information, and citation text are edited. Most technical prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: The fixed-input table moves from main-text Table 3 to appendix Table 5; complexity and hyperparameter tables are renumbered. Figures and appendix tables shift with reflow, while all six figures and the table designs retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens literature coverage and removes an unresolved citation marker, with little added comparative synthesis. The method, proofs, numerical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Moving the fixed-input control to Appendix D.3 reduces its prominence while preserving access through a cross-reference. These contextual and editorial changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
